rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.outlines.OutlineItem`.

**Constructor defaults.** The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments]` builds an item with `OutlineItem::new`. It asserts that `name_span` is `None` and `attachments` is empty. This covers "`OutlineItem::new` initializes the list to empty" and the `name_span` default of `None` from the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.name_span`.

**Builders.** The test then calls `with_name_span(Span::new(7, 8))`. It calls `with_attachments` twice, first with a `Comment` attachment and then with an `Annotation` attachment. After the second call it asserts that exactly one attachment remains, with kind `Annotation` and span `4..6`. A "sets" implementation passes, and an implementation that appends or ignores the argument fails. Replacement is the right reading of "sets it to the supplied list".

**Field preservation.** After `item.clone()`, the item is wrapped in an `Outline` that is then cloned. A tuple assertion checks that `selector`, `kind`, `span` and `structural_hash` equal `"fn[f]"`, `"fn"`, `Span::new(2, 12)` and `"digest"`. The test also asserts `name_span == Some(Span::new(7, 8))`. This covers all six public fields, and it confirms that `Clone` preserves them.

**Traits and exports.** `Clone` is exercised directly. `Debug` is checked only through `format!("{outline:?}")`, which is non-empty, and that format compiles only if `OutlineItem` implements `Debug`. The test does not format an `OutlineItem` directly, but the trait obligation carries no further behavior. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` is also marked. It checks that the exported paths and item kinds match the specification.

**Delegated obligations.** The meaning of `span`, the choice of highlighted name text, and which item owns each attachment belong to the cited requirements `Span`, `name_span` and `attachments`. Those cited requirements need no test here.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior in the subject's own obligations that these tests would accept.

`trust_but_verify::outline::Span` locates text by byte offsets from the start
of the original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item.
`start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive. A valid span satisfies
`start <= end <= source.len()` and both offsets are UTF-8 character boundaries.
For `source: &str`, `&source[span]` yields the same slice as
`&source[span.start..span.end]`, with the same bounds and boundary checks.
pub fn new(start: usize, end: usize) -> Self;
A named item's `name_span` is `Some` with the span to highlight for its name
in the original source snapshot. The highlighted text may differ from the
name in the selector. Use `selector` to address the item. The file root and
anonymous items have `name_span` set to `None`. `OutlineItem::new` starts with
`None`. Language providers use `with_name_span` to set the highlight within
